significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "high-surprise, low-teacher-probability tokens recover oracle divergence tokens," that suppressing their gradients causally reduces trait transmission, and that targeting early layers is sufficient: P1 is a form-(iii) predictive coupling, while P2 and P3 are form-(ii) causal/mechanistic claims. This fixes expectations about which tokens carry hidden traits and which training updates can block them across several behaviors, addressing the specific hidden-carrier and filtering problem exposed by Cloud et al.'s "Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data" rather than merely showing subliminal learning again; it establishes both a carrier phenomenon and a mechanism-linked defense. The branches are determinate and informative: failure of P1 rules out surprise as a single-teacher carrier proxy, failure of P2 despite P1 shows that detecting carriers is insufficient for immunization, and failure of P3 rejects early-layer sufficiency. In the topic-substitution check, replacing these specific claims with only "extend research on subliminal learning" would not merit this score; the increment comes from the measurable proxy relation and linked causal suppression, which are sharper than the topic's obvious first hypothesis of locating or masking carrier tokens.

reach.justification: The named handles are the per-token "surprise s_i = -log p_teacher(x_i | context)" diagnostic and "Divergence-Token Regularization (DTR)" intervention; these are ex ante because they flag and attenuate candidate carriers during training, before the resulting student trait is deployed or elicited. After per-model threshold calibration, the conclusion predicts that high-surprise tokens will be enriched for divergence carriers and that early-layer suppression will retain a favorable suppression-utility relation, so more than a mere search procedure transfers, although the stated high-probability-token adaptive attack bounds that transfer. The asserted scope covers single-teacher distillation, multiple traits, matched and mismatched bases, and two model families, with downstream uptake by practitioners who "insert it as a default stage when distilling from untrusted third-party teachers," not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: subliminal learning alone supplies neither an ex-ante screen nor a training-time knob, whereas the surprise statistic and DTR do.
